content: The primary ROI metric. heading: 5.2 Licensing — What You Get with Copilot
content: Every M365 Copilot licence automatically includes the Viva Insights service plan at no additional cost. That bundled plan contributes to Viva Insights eligibility, but each capability still has its own assigned-plan threshold, role, access, data, cloud, and preview requirements. A separate Viva Insights purchase is needed when the measured population includes employees who do not receive the bundled plan through Copilot.

heading: 5.3 Privacy by Design
content: Group-level by default: Copilot Dashboard views are aggregated at group level. Identification is a separate capability, controlled by its own Viva feature access management (VFAM) policy, that can surface named employees in the Consumption Dashboard and in data exports Minimum group size: Default 10 (configurable down to 5) Differential privacy: Microsoft documents it for Viva Insights organization insights (manager and leader views); the Copilot Dashboard article does not state that it applies to dashboard metrics Exclusion lists: Hide specific users from the aggregated insights in the Copilot Dashboard, Agent Dashboard, Consumption Dashboard and Viva Insights collaboration reports. This is a reporting control, not a statement that their data is never processed

heading: 2. What Breaks with an Incomplete Entra ID Hierarchy?
content: If the Entra ID Manager attribute is missing or inconsistent for many users: Feature Impact Auto CxO Identification Fewer leaders are auto-identified. Users without a clear reporting line are excluded from the "top 3 levels" calculation. Manager Settings (team-level data) Managers without a populated Manager attribute or without enough direct reports won't see team-level data. Filter by manager hierarchy (Publish Reports) Published reports with "Filter by manager hierarchy" will show incomplete data. Advanced Analytics cohort segmentation Manager-based grouping will be inaccurate. Recommendation: If more than 20% of users lack a Manager attribute, prioritise fixing directory data or supplement with an org data CSV upload that includes correct ManagerId values.

heading: 3. Source Precedence Is Surface- and Attribute-Specific
content: An upload changes the source for the attributes supplied to the apps you select; it does not universally or permanently replace Microsoft Entra ID across Microsoft 365. (Microsoft's Copilot Dashboard article says an upload permanently changes the dashboard data source from Entra ID to the data file; the parallel-ingestion article describes sourcing ManagerId and Organization from Entra alongside uploaded data.) Surface / attribute Controlling behaviour Operational rule Microsoft 365 User Profile Microsoft Entra is the default source. Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service (formerly Organizational Data in Microsoft 365) can be prioritised; when Entra is missing or incomplete, uploaded data can fill gaps. Keep Profile precedence at Entra unless there is an approved reason to override it. Copilot Dashboard and Viva Insights Uploaded data shared with these apps supplies the mapped dashboard and analysis attributes. If both Viva and Microsoft 365 uploads exist, Microsoft documents a merge with the more recent upload taking priority. Document the owner and source for every supplied attribute; verify values in Dashboard filters and Viva data quality after each change. Viva ManagerId...

heading: Supported correction and rollback paths
content: Update: Upload only affected users and all attributes you intend to change. A blank value preserves the existing value because new uploads merge with previous data. Delete a value: Use the documented type-specific marker: two single quotes ( '' ) in CSV for strings (three in Excel), -1 for integers, a nonexistent in-tenant address for email values, or 01-01-0001 for dates. Correct history: Use Historical import with a CSV and a File valid as of date. Microsoft documents historical updates for Viva Insights data only. Return ManagerId / Organization to Entra: Enable those attributes under Configure Entra connection , then delete uploaded optional attributes you no longer need. Migration failure: Stop further imports and open a Microsoft support request. Microsoft documents temporary rollback only for critical migration issues in special cases. Do Not Use a Dummy-Row Rollback Do not use a one-row "Replace All" file as a general removal or rollback technique. It can leave an artificial hierarchy and break filters, partitions, or reports. Use the supported update/delete markers, parallel Entra restoration, or Microsoft Support instead. Microsoft's FAQ for admin center uploads separa...

heading: Microsoft 365 Copilot Analytics
content: Why Multi-Agency Analytics Is Hard The architectural challenge of scoping analytics across agencies in a shared tenant Document Property Value Section Explain Audience CIO, Solution Architect Version 4.2 Last validated 2 October 2026

heading: When This Applies
content: Multi-agency analytics is a challenge when your organisation meets all of the following conditions: Single M365 tenant — all agencies share one tenant Multiple independent agencies (or business units, divisions, departments) that operate semi-autonomously Each agency needs Copilot analytics scoped to their own population The fundamental tension: Microsoft 365 Copilot analytics has several separately governed surfaces. In a shared tenant, there is no single partition or product setting that scopes the Copilot Dashboard, Agent Dashboard, metrics export, delegation, manager access, analyst queries, privileged roles, and downstream Power BI sharing together. A user with a tenant-wide access source can see "Your company" data even when an agency analyst is assigned only to an agency partition. The patterns below coordinate those independent controls. They reduce accidental cross-agency reporting, but they do not create cryptographic, tenant, or product security isolation. Single-Agency Tenants If your tenant serves only one agency (or your agencies don't need separate analytics scoping), none of this applies. Follow the standard Admin Setup Guide instead.

heading: The Two Architectures
content: THIS GUIDE'S AUTHOR-CREATED ARCHITECTURE PATTERNS Default Priority and Restricted Reporting (formerly labelled "Isolation" in this guide and retained in existing URLs) are editorial names created by this guide. They are not Microsoft product, security, compliance, or licensing terms. Microsoft documents the component capabilities, including partitions; Microsoft does not document this guide's combined pattern as an end-to-end security boundary. Default Priority is the simpler author-created option. An agency leader's "Your group" scope can follow their Entra ID manager hierarchy when Microsoft's access and hierarchy conditions are met (Microsoft does not state which scope the dashboard opens to, so confirm the landing scope in the tenant). The trade-off is intentional: a user with a tenant-wide access source may still use "Your company", and a senior leader who has company-level access and is a manager chooses each delegate's scope: "Your group", "Your company" or "Combined access". Combined access includes the Consumption Dashboard, and a delegate with it sees exactly what the delegator sees. A delegate can't delegate further, the maximum is 75 delegates, and delegates must als...

content: Dimension Default Priority Restricted Reporting Core principle Agency CEOs can see their team through the "Your group" scope via manager hierarchy (landing scope: confirm in the tenant) Partition-scoped analyst queries plus separate access and delivery controls Cross-agency visibility Possible — users can navigate to "Your company" Reduced by surface-specific controls; residual tenant-wide and privileged access remains Partitions needed No Yes — one per agency Report delivery Native Copilot Dashboard Power BI workspaces (recommended) PowerShell required No Yes (VFAM lockdown only; partitions are created via UI) Setup effort 2–4 hours 1–3 days Best for Organisations where cross-agency visibility is acceptable Organisations that accept defense-in-depth reporting segmentation after risk and compliance review

heading: Surface-by-Actor Boundary Matrix
content: Actor and surface What the pattern controls Residual risk / required control Agency leader or manager — Copilot Dashboard Default Priority uses manager scope; Restricted Reporting can target the agency-user group with web-app/VFAM restrictions. A shared executive or cross-agency manager hierarchy can span agencies. A tenant-wide access grant or eligible delegation can broaden scope. Test each role and account directly. heading: 6. Post-Upload Verification Checklist

Re-submit if needed.

heading: Step 2: Download Import Log
content: Look for rows with unmatched Microsoft_ManagerEmail values. These indicate managers whose email addresses don't exist in the uploaded data or in Entra ID.

heading: Step 3: Download Manager Log
content: This log shows employees whose ManagerEmail doesn't resolve to an active user in Entra ID. These employees will appear as "orphaned" in the manager hierarchy.

heading: Step 4: Check Attribute Coverage
content: Open the Data overview page (or the validation details under Data Connections ). Use an organization-approved acceptance threshold; this guide uses >95% coverage for critical segmentation attributes as an operational target, not as a Microsoft product requirement. Investigate any material drop from the pre-change baseline, because missing values can exclude people from filtered views.

heading: Step 5: Check Manager Tree Count
content: The number of root nodes in the manager hierarchy should be small (typically 1–5, representing CEO/top executives). If you see hundreds or thousands, many ManagerEmail values are missing or incorrect.

heading: 1. Privacy Thresholds
content: Privacy thresholds protect aggregated organization insights ; they do not turn every Viva Insights output into aggregate-only data. Insights Analysts can receive de-identified row-level employee records in advanced analysis, and uploaded organizational attributes can make a person inferable when combined. Identification, a separate capability, lets authorised users see named employees ("identified outputs") in Consumption Dashboard insights and exports and in the Copilot Dashboard and Agent Dashboard data exports (listed as private preview; Microsoft's Agent Dashboard export article says public preview, so validate in the tenant). Setting Default Configurable Range Minimum group size 10 users 5–unlimited (lowest allowed = 5)

heading: How Thresholds Work
content: Data suppression: Results for groups below the threshold are not shown, so potentially identifiable information is not displayed. Dashboard and manager/leader insights: These surfaces use protected aggregates, minimum group size, distribution masking, and differential privacy where documented. Advanced analysis: An Insights Analyst can query de-identified individual-level organizational and Microsoft 365 metrics. The encrypted person identifier is not a guarantee of anonymity if title, location, organization, or custom attributes enable inference. Access governance: Treat analyst output as potentially personal data. Use least-privilege partitions, require role-specific privacy/security training, define an approved analysis purpose, and audit authored queries against policy and any data protection impact assessment. Identification: Copilot Analytics outputs are de-identified by default. Identification lets authorised users see named employees ("identified outputs"). Microsoft lists it for Consumption Dashboard insights and data export, and lists Copilot Dashboard and Agent Dashboard data exports as private preview. heading: 4. GDPR and Regional Compliance

Data minimisation: Dashboards and manager/leader insights use protected aggregates; advanced-analysis queries can contain de-identified individual rows; identified outputs, where an administrator enables Identification, can name employees. Limit attributes, rows, retention, and query purpose to what the approved analysis requires. Org data handling: If you upload organisational data (CSV with attributes like Department, Agency, Location), ensure the upload process follows your organisation's data handling policies. Do not include sensitive personal data in org data attributes.

heading: 1. Copilot Dashboard Pages
content: The Copilot Dashboard is accessible at insights.cloud.microsoft and is divided into three main pages: Readiness , Adoption , and Impact , each with a Sentiment section; a Learning tab carries Microsoft research. Each page answers a different question about your organisation's Copilot deployment.

heading: 1.1 Readiness Page
content: The Readiness page answers: "How many Copilot licences have we assigned, how many users are active, and what should we enable next?" "Copilot licenses assigned" and "Active Copilot users" — the metrics in the "Activate Copilot for your organization" section summarise progress towards activating Copilot. Tenant-level counts include disabled mailboxes; group-level counts do not. Managers do not have access to the Readiness page, and delegates do not see this section. heading: 1.2 Adoption Page
content: The Adoption page answers: "Who is using Copilot, how often, and in which apps?"

heading: Key Metrics
content: Metric Definition Active Copilot users Number of licensed users who had at least one Copilot interaction in the 28-day measurement window. Copilot Actions Taken Total count of Copilot actions across supported Microsoft 365 apps and Copilot Chat. Agent adoption is reported separately in the Agent Dashboard, but Microsoft states that Teams Facilitator and Interpreter agent usage is included in overall usage metrics. Usage Intensity Average number of actions per active user (Actions Taken ÷ Active Users). Measures depth of engagement beyond simple headcount. Returning users Users who took at least one Copilot action in both the current and the preceding period (monthly or weekly toggle). Shows sustained adoption rather than one-time trial. Usage levels Power, Habitual, Novice and Other users, classified over a rolling 12-week window — see Usage Levels (Power Users) below. Internal Benchmark An additional adoption trendline for "a group of similar employees within your company". Select Show benchmark to display it. External Benchmark Compares your adoption trends with "Copilot usage at other companies similar to yours". Helps answer "Are we ahead or behind?"

heading: Usage Levels (Power Users)
content: The Adoption page classifies licensed users over a rolling 12-week window. In the section that analyses the drivers of power usage, the gear icon at the top right of the Frequent usage card lets you customise the number of actions used to group users. Level Definition (Microsoft) Power users Average 15 or more Copilot actions per week and used Copilot in at least 9 of the past 12 weeks Habitual users Average between 1 and 14 Copilot actions per week and used Copilot in at least 9 of the past 12 weeks Novice users Average at least 1 Copilot action in the past 12 weeks and did not use Copilot in at least 9 of the past 12 weeks Other users Licensed users who meet none of the criteria above, including users who have not yet used Copilot in the measurement window Microsoft's Supported environments matrix lists power users metrics as available in Worldwide, not available in GCC Moderate and partial in GCC High.

These help you understand how people use Copilot, not just how much . Intent Category What It Captures Example Prompts Ask and find Questions and information retrieval "Find the recording of meeting X from May", "Who is the project lead for initiative Y?" Catch up Summaries, recaps, and action items "Recap this meeting with key takeaways", "Summarise what happened while I was out" Draft and brainstorm Content generation and creative ideation "Draft a status update email about project X", "Brainstorm creative presentation ideas" Other Prompts that don't fit the above categories General questions, casual interactions Microsoft's metric reference lists the four intent metrics (Ask and find, Catch up, Draft and brainstorm, other) for the Copilot Dashboard but does not mark them as available in Advanced analysis. The manager hierarchy chain must include a row for every manager between the leader and their reports. Verify that your CSV (or Entra Manager field) has rows for every intermediate manager. heading: Export Copilot Metrics Safely (Preview)
content: The Copilot metrics export is a preview feature with a fixed, non-customizable schema. It exports user-level metric rows (anonymised by default), not the aggregated chart currently visible on screen.

heading: Prerequisites
content: The tenant must meet the documented 50-licence threshold. Because Microsoft pages conflict on mixed service-plan counting, verify assigned service plans and export availability in the tenant. The exporter must have global / Your company access . A manager or "Your group" delegate cannot export. The Copilot Metrics Export feature must be enabled for the user, and the capability must be available in the tenant's cloud. It is not available in GCC Moderate or GCC High according to Microsoft's Supported environments matrix.

heading: How to Export
content: Open the Copilot Dashboard in the Viva Insights web app. Select the Copilot metrics Export control. Choose Week for weekly rows covering the past six months or Day for daily rows covering the past 28 days. Download the CSV and record the export date, granularity, source article date, and tenant/cloud used.

heading: What's in the Export
content: Property Correct interpretation Grain and period One user-level record per time interval (anonymised by default): up to six months for Week, or 28 days for Day. Identity De-identified by default : personal identifiers are replaced with anonymised IDs, so the export is user-level data, not aggregate-only data. When identifiable export is enabled for a user, their export includes identifiable fields. Microsoft lists Identification for the Copilot Dashboard data export (private preview); access is governed by a dedicated Viva feature access management (VFAM) policy, which only a Microsoft 365 Global Administrator or an AI Administrator can create. Customization The schema and metric selection are not customizable, and Dashboard filters/groupings do not redefine the export. Metrics The documented export metrics are provided in the fixed schema. Copilot Assisted Hours is not included. Day-level exports also omit the meeting-recap and meeting-summary metrics. Zero values can appear because the export covers users with and without a Copilot licence; use Total Copilot enabled days to identify enabled users.

heading: Privacy Handling
content: Treat the CSV as sensitive analytics data even though direct identities are removed by default (an export with identifiable export enabled contains personal data); repeated user-level rows and joins with organizational data can increase re-identification risk. Store it in an access-controlled location, apply retention and sensitivity requirements, restrict downstream joins, and document every recipient and purpose. Do not present row-level data or attempt re-identification. Aggregate under approved minimum-group and privacy rules before wider distribution. Validate row counts, dates, granularity, metric definitions, missing values, and diagnostic-data coverage before publishing trends. Export vs Advanced Analytics The preview export provides a fixed user-level dataset (anonymised by default). Use Advanced Reporting when an Insights Analyst needs governed metric selection, partition-scoped queries, or custom segmentation. Neither route removes the need for privacy review. Source: Export Copilot metrics from the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard (Last updated 15 July 2026).

heading: 1.4 Sentiment Section
content: The Sentiment section appears on the Readiness, Adoption and Impact pages and shows qualitative user feedback about Copilot. Component What It Shows Notes Sentiment results by question Aggregated responses to Copilot experience questions Includes benchmark comparison against similar orgs Sentiment by group Heat map showing sentiment across organisational groups Viva Insights customers only — requires Viva Insights licence Manager team view Sentiment breakdown for a manager's direct reports Subject to minimum group size suppression No Survey Data? If no survey data has been uploaded, or the minimum privacy threshold is not met, the Sentiment section shows no survey responses. This is expected. The Satisfaction Rate metric (thumbs up/down) works independently of surveys, but it appears only when there are at least 30 feedback responses from at least five unique users in the rolling 28-day period; otherwise the card says there is not enough feedback.

heading: 2. How to Delegate Access
content: Dashboard access can be shared with others through delegation. This is how leaders give their managers or analysts visibility into Copilot usage for their scope.

heading: Three Methods to Add Delegates
content: Method Steps Method 1: Settings Viva Insights web app → Settings (left navigation) → Delegation → Add delegates → enter name(s) → Confirm Method 2: Share Copilot Dashboard or Agent Dashboard → Share (top right) → Add delegates → enter name(s) → Confirm Method 3: Reports page Reports page → Add delegates → enter name(s) → Confirm A senior leader who has company-level access and is a manager chooses each delegate's scope: Your group , Your company or Combined access . Combined access includes the Consumption Dashboard, and a delegate with it sees exactly what the delegator sees. A delegate can't delegate further. The maximum is 75 delegates. Delegates must also be permitted to use the dashboard. If the delegator has both company-level and group access, existing "Your company" delegates automatically become Combined access and might see the Consumption Dashboard. Review delegate scopes after this change. See Microsoft's Delegate access article.

heading: 3. Step-by-Step: Create a Report
content: This walkthrough uses the Microsoft Copilot impact report template as the example, but the process is similar for all templates.

heading: Step 1 — Sign In to the Analyst Experience
content: Navigate to analysis.insights.cloud.microsoft and sign in with your organisational account that has the Insights Analyst role.

heading: Step 2 — Start a New Analysis
content: Select Create analysis → Templates → Copilot → choose the desired template (e.g., Microsoft Copilot impact report ) → Set up analysis .

heading: Step 3 — Configure Query Settings
content: Set the following: Query name — use a descriptive name (e.g., "Copilot Impact Q1 2026 — All Agencies") Time period — select the analysis window (up to 13 months of historical data) Auto-refresh — enable if you want the query to re-run automatically on a schedule Description — optional but recommended for team documentation

heading: Step 4 — Review Predefined Metrics
content: The template pre-selects the required metrics (shown as grey tags — these cannot be removed). You can optionally add extra metrics to include in the query output.

heading: Step 5 — Set Employee Filters
content: Apply filters to scope the query population: "Is Active" — not available when a query includes Copilot metrics (Microsoft: you can't use the "Is Active" filter when analysing Copilot metrics); it remains a predefined filter in the behavioural-only collaboration templates Org attributes — filter by department, agency, location, or any uploaded org data attribute as needed

heading: Step 6 — Add Organisational Attributes
content: Select up to 20 organisational attributes to include in the query output. These attributes become available as group-by and filter dimensions in Power BI. Include any attribute you may want to slice by later — you cannot add them after the query runs.

heading: Step 7 — Run the Query
content: Select Run . Microsoft says a template query might take a few minutes to run; larger populations and longer time windows can take longer. You will receive a notification when results are ready. Data Quality Warnings During query setup, the system may flag data quality issues: Yellow warning — low quality or partial coverage for an attribute. The query will still run. Red warning — missing attribute entirely. The query will run but that attribute will not be usable for segmentation. Address data quality issues by working with your Insights Admin to update the org data upload.

heading: 4. Connect Power BI
content: Once your query completes, connect it to the Power BI template:

heading: Step 1 — Download the Template
content: From the query results page in Viva Insights, download the .pbit template file.

heading: Step 2 — Open in Power BI Desktop
content: Open the downloaded .pbit file in Power BI Desktop. When prompted, paste: Partition ID — found in the Viva Insights analyst experience Query ID — found on the query results page

heading: Step 3 — Set Minimum Group Size
content: Set the minimum group size for privacy thresholds (e.g., 10). Groups smaller than this threshold will be suppressed in the report. Click Load .

heading: Step 4 — Sign In
content: When prompted for credentials, select Organisational account and sign in with the same account used to run the query.

heading: Step 5 — Configure Report Settings
content: After data loads, configure the report settings on the Settings page: Time period — define the reporting window within the query's date range Group-by attribute — select the primary organisational attribute for segmentation (e.g., Department, Agency) Active user definition — set the threshold for what constitutes an "active" Copilot user Language — set report language

heading: 7.1 Publish via Viva Insights
content: You can share query results with business leaders directly from Viva Insights using the Publish feature. This is the fastest route for leaders who already have Copilot Dashboard access. Microsoft documents the feature in Publish reports .

heading: Step 1 — Select Publish
content: In the Viva Insights analyst experience, navigate to your completed query and select Publish .

heading: Step 2 — Set Report Metadata
content: Enter: Title — the report title that recipients will see Publisher name — your name or team name Description — brief summary of what the report covers

heading: Step 3 — Choose Scope
content: Select one of: Unfiltered original — publishes the full dataset. All recipients see the same data. Filter by manager hierarchy — each recipient sees only data for their reporting line.

heading: Step 4 — Set Expiry Date
content: Set when the published report expires. Maximum is 365 days from publication.

heading: Step 5 — Publish
content: Confirm and publish. Recipients receive an email notification with a link to view the report. No Documented Notification Before Expiry Microsoft does not document a notification before a published report expires, so set a calendar reminder to re-publish before the expiry date to avoid gaps in leader access. Multi-Agency Tenants: Manager Hierarchy Risk Enabling a manager so they can receive a published report also grants them Copilot Dashboard access scoped to their own group ("Your group"). Company-wide ("Your company") access, which shows aggregated data across all agencies, comes from other routes — automatic senior-leader access from Entra ID data, the Global Administrator role, assigned global access, or a company-scoped delegate — so check who already holds it before relying on Publish in a multi-agency tenant. For agency-head delivery, use Power BI sharing (Section 7.2) instead, and reserve Viva Insights Publish for Central IT who already have tenant-wide dashboard access. See the Multi-Agency Setup Guide and the Restricted Reporting playbook (Phase 4b).

heading: 7.2 Share via Power BI
content: Unlike Publish via Viva Insights (Section 7.1) , which distributes results natively inside Viva Insights, this method uses Power BI's own sharing . It is the preferred method for multi-agency tenants because it delivers a report to named people without granting them any Copilot Dashboard access — whereas 7.1's "Filter by manager hierarchy" option can (see its warning). New to Power BI? Start Here This section assumes an Insights Analyst has already built the report in Sections 1–4 (run a query, connect the template, save the file). If you are an admin handling only distribution , you can start at Step 1 below with a report file the analyst hands you. Three Power BI terms used in this section: .pbix — the finished report file. When the analyst loads data into the .pbit template (Section 4) and saves it, it becomes a .pbix . That is the file you publish. Workspace — a shared container in the Power BI service that holds reports and controls who can see them. Dataset — the data behind a report; publishing a .pbix uploads the report and its dataset together.

heading: Step 1 — Publish the .pbix to the Power BI Service
content: In Power BI Desktop, select Publish and choose a destination workspace (not "My workspace", which can't be shared with others). The report and its dataset upload to app.powerbi.com .

heading: Step 2 — Use a Dedicated Workspace per Audience
content: Create one workspace per agency or audience (e.g., Agency A — Copilot Analytics ). Keeping each agency's reports in a separate workspace is the cleanest way to control who sees what. Store all .pbix files here rather than on individual machines so reporting survives staff changes.

heading: Step 3 — Assign Stakeholders via Workspace Roles
content: In app.powerbi.com , open the workspace → select Manage access → Add people or groups , then assign a workspace role from the table below. Prefer adding an Entra security group over individuals, so access is managed centrally and consistently with your other governance controls. Role Can do Assign to Viewer View and interact with reports only Most stakeholders (agency leaders) Contributor Create/edit content; can't manage access Co-analysts who build reports Member Edit content and add others (below Admin) Trusted leads who help run the workspace Admin Full control, including deleting the workspace The owning analyst / Central IT Cleaner Distribution for Wide Audiences For a large, read-only audience, publish the workspace as a Power BI app — a packaged, read-only view of selected reports (not a desktop or mobile application). Give the audience access to the app rather than the workspace, so recipients get a curated view without seeing the underlying workspace contents.

heading: Step 4 — Confirm Viewer Licensing
content: Power BI sharing is licensed separately from Viva Insights and Copilot: Each viewer needs a Power BI Pro or Premium Per User (PPU) licence; or if the workspace sits on a Power BI Premium (P SKU) or Fabric F64-or-larger capacity , viewers with a free licence and the Viewer role can view the reports — removing per-viewer costs. F SKUs smaller than F64 still require a Pro or PPU licence for each viewer. Confirm with your licensing owner. Multi-Agency: Keep Boundaries Intact Grant each agency workspace's Viewer role only to that agency's leaders — via an agency-scoped Entra group. If multiple agencies must share one workspace, add Row-Level Security (RLS) as a secondary control. The full agency-isolation delivery procedure (including the Publish Reports pitfall) is in the Restricted Reporting playbook , Phase 4b.

heading: 8. Ongoing Maintenance
content: Keep your Copilot analytics current with these recurring tasks: Refresh org data monthly — work with your Insights Admin to ensure organisational data (new hires, transfers, departures) stays up to date. heading: Credit Mechanics
content: Credits reset monthly — there is no rollover of unused credits to the next month. Overage behaviour: Microsoft allows some overage; custom agents are disabled when a tenant reaches 125% of prepaid capacity (ongoing conversations are not interrupted), and new agent flow runs are blocked when prepaid capacity is exhausted. Environments configured to bill overage to pay-as-you-go are handled through the Azure subscription. Credits are pooled at the tenant level for prepaid plans, or billed per-environment for pay-as-you-go .

heading: 7. Multi-Agency Chargeback Model
content: For organisations with multiple agencies, departments, or cost centres, a chargeback model distributes Copilot costs to the consuming business units.

heading: Option A: Org Data–Based Attribution
content: Upload org data with an Agency (or CostCentre ) attribute through the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Viva Insights web app, as applicable to your tenant (check Message Center). Export the Copilot Credits report filtered by user from the M365 Admin Center. Join user-level consumption data with org data to map each user's credit usage to their agency. Aggregate by agency to produce the chargeback summary.

heading: Option B: Separate Billing Policies
content: Create separate billing policies in PPAC — one per agency. Link each billing policy to a different Azure subscription or cost centre. Assign environments to the appropriate billing policy based on the owning agency. Each agency's Azure subscription is billed directly for their consumption.

heading: Quarterly Reconciliation Process
content: At the end of each quarter, export consumption data from both PPAC and M365 Admin Center. The admin center credits report covers only unlicensed Copilot Chat users on pay-as-you-go and at most 30 days, so rely on PPAC for the full quarter. Reconcile prepaid credit consumption against allocations per agency. Reconcile pay-as-you-go charges against Azure invoices. Review and adjust allocations based on actual usage trends. Produce a chargeback summary report for finance teams. Note: Option B (separate billing policies) provides cleaner cost separation but requires more administrative overhead. Option A is simpler to maintain for organisations with fewer than 10 agencies. Agent billing and capacity: For Copilot Credit billing rates, enforcement and capacity management, see Microsoft's Billing rates and management article and the Microsoft Copilot Studio Licensing Guide it links to.

heading: Scenario 1: Meeting Culture Audit
content: Template: Meeting Effectiveness Goal: Identify meeting overload, long recurring meetings, and multitasking patterns across the organisation. Approach: Run the Meeting Effectiveness template with a 6-month time window. Analyse metrics: recurring meeting hours, meetings > 60 minutes, multitasking hours. Group by department or business unit to identify hotspots. Calculate potential time savings: if average employee spends 4 hours/week in meetings that could be emails, that's X hours reclaimed per person per week. Outcome: Data-driven recommendations to reclaim meeting time, backed by actual behavioural data rather than surveys.

heading: Scenario 2: Wellbeing Baseline Before Copilot Rollout
content: Template: Wellbeing – Balance & Flexibility Goal: Capture focus time, after-hours work, and work-life balance metrics before Copilot deployment. Then compare after 3 months using the Copilot Impact template. Approach: Run the Wellbeing template covering the 4 weeks immediately before Copilot licence assignment. Record the baseline period and cohort before comparing post-deployment results; see the Analyst Playbook: Business Impact setup and interpretation . Record baseline metrics: average focus hours, after-hours collaboration hours, weekend work hours. After 3 months of Copilot usage, run the Copilot Impact template for the same population. Compare pre- and post-deployment metrics to quantify Copilot's impact on employee wellbeing. Outcome: Quantifiable evidence of whether Copilot improved, maintained, or negatively affected employee wellbeing metrics.

heading: Scenario 3: Manager Effectiveness Programme
content: Template: Manager Effectiveness Goal: Identify managers with low 1:1 time or high span of control. Feed insights into leadership development initiatives. Approach: Run the Manager Effectiveness template for the past 6 months. Analyse metrics: manager 1:1 meeting hours, team size (span of control), team after-hours patterns. Filter to managers with fewer than 30 minutes of 1:1 time per direct report per month. Cross-reference with team wellbeing metrics to identify teams with both low manager engagement and high after-hours work. Outcome: Targeted list of managers who would benefit from coaching programmes, with behavioural evidence to support the recommendation.

heading: Step 1 — Open Insights and confirm scope
content: Open the Viva Insights web app and select the Consumption Dashboard . heading: Step 2 — Read the summary cards
content: Metric Operational meaning Validation question Active users Unique users who took at least one action in Copilot Cowork or the Work IQ API Did covered activity occur in this scope during the current month? Total Copilot credit usage Credits consumed by covered activity in the selected scope Does the direction align with the official billing view, allowing for scope and timing? heading: Step 3 — Analyze trends and service drivers
content: Use the trend controls to change the plotted metric, break it down by group, organization, or job function, and choose the available date granularity. Then use the service breakdown to identify which covered service and employee segment account for the largest share. Treat this as a prioritization signal, then validate against service ownership and business context.

heading: Step 4 — Review usage intensity
content: Usage intensity shows whether consumption is broadly distributed or concentrated. Review these segments: All users Top 1 percent of users Top 5 percent of users Top 6–25 percent of users Top 26–50 percent of users For each segment, compare total credits, average credits per user, average credits per session, average sessions per user, and active users. A concentrated distribution is a prompt to investigate workload design, automation, value, and policy fit; it is not by itself evidence of misuse.

heading: Step 5 — Review spending-policy limits
content: Use the spending-policy table to identify the top policies in use, average credits used per user, the displayed spending limit, and the number of users near or at that limit. Microsoft defines "near or at" as users who have used at least 90 percent of the credits allowed by their spending policy limit; spending policy limits are set in the Microsoft 365 admin center and reset on the first day of each month. Contact the policy owner before users are depleted. The dashboard reports the condition; policy configuration and capacity enforcement occur in the relevant administration and billing surfaces. Capacity has contractual and service consequences Copilot Studio documentation states that purchased capacity is enforced monthly, unused Copilot Credits do not carry over, and exceeding purchased capacity can lead to technical enforcement and service denial. Confirm the applicable licensing model, included usage, zero-rated scenarios, and current terms in the official licensing and Copilot Credit guides before taking purchasing or enforcement action.

heading: 5. Export and Reconciliation
content: The Consumption Dashboard export is a public-preview feature for user-level AI cost metrics. Personal identifiers are hashed unless an administrator has enabled identifiable export for you, in which case the export also includes identifiable fields. It is currently available to Insights Analysts with global partition access and Microsoft 365 Global Administrators . Microsoft's articles differ on manager export: the export article says data export for managers "will be available by the end of July" (a date that has passed), while the Manager settings article says managers granted Consumption insights can access team-scoped data in the dashboard "and export data". heading: Worked example — the executive sponsor who isn't a manager
content: This case comes up constantly, so it's worth walking through end-to-end because the intuitive answer is the wrong one. The situation The executive sponsor of the organisation's Copilot rollout needs the org-wide adoption report to track the programme. The sponsor is not a people-manager — with no direct reports — and holds no admin role. The instinctive move is "they're an exec, just give them manager access." That doesn't work, and it's worth understanding why. Why "manager" is the wrong lever. In Viva Insights, "manager" is not a statement about seniority or importance — it is a literal test of whether the person has direct or indirect reports , established by the PersonId / ManagerId hierarchy. You cannot enable someone as a manager who has nobody reporting to them, no matter how senior they are. And even if the sponsor did have a small team, manager access would only show that team's adoption — not the company-wide view an executive sponsor actually needs. The correct lever here is delegation. heading: 1. Executive Summary
content: This document provides an author-created, defense-in-depth reporting pattern for Microsoft Copilot Dashboard and Copilot Analytics in a single Microsoft 365 tenant that hosts multiple agencies . It coordinates product controls to reduce cross-agency reporting paths; it does not establish an end-to-end security boundary. Core Constraint & Key Finding: The design objective is to prevent routine agency-facing reporting paths from exposing another agency's data. The Copilot Dashboard and other tenant surfaces are governed separately from analyst partitions, and some access sources can remain tenant-wide. Therefore the objective must be expressed and tested per actor and surface rather than as an absolute guarantee. Recommended Approach: Two Coordinated Reporting Layers Viva Insights Advanced Analytics with Partitions — for row/column-scoped agency analyst query workspaces. Copilot Dashboard with controlled access — for tenant-level oversight by central IT only (secondary, restricted use). Power BI workspaces/apps — a separate agency-facing delivery layer with Viewer-first permissions, sharing/export controls, and optional RLS.

heading: 4.1 Choose Your Path: CSV Org Data vs. Entra ID Domain
content: Viva Insights partitions filter on organizational data attributes . Attributes reach Viva Insights from two sources: Source Attributes Available Setup Required Microsoft Entra ID (automatic sync) PersonId , ManagerId , Organization (from Entra Department field), plus system-generated: Domain (from SMTP), TimeZone , PopulationType None — syncs automatically. Optionally enable ManagerId/Organization via "Configure Entra connection" CSV Org Data Upload All of the above, plus up to 100 optional attributes (105 attributes in total): Agency , FunctionType , Location , LevelDesignation , CostCentre , etc. Record current source precedence, then use Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service unless the tenant UI and Message Center explicitly expose a supported legacy path. Workday has a 100,000-user limit; API-based import is preview and environment-dependent.

heading: Path A: CSV Org Data Upload (Full Capability)
content: Use when: All agencies share the same email domain (e.g., everyone is @onetenant.gov.au ) You need both agency analyst query segmentation and department/location/job-function filtering You want the richest possible analytics (custom attributes, before/after cohort segmentation) HR can provide a consolidated employee CSV with an Agency column Partition filter: Agency = "Agency A" End-to-end workflow: Phase 0: Pre-flight audit (same as Path B) Phase 1: Lockdown — disable AutoCxO, delegation, Agent Dashboard, Metrics Export (same as Path B) Phase 2: Prepare and upload CSV with Microsoft_PersonEmail , Microsoft_ManagerEmail , Microsoft_Organization and the custom Agency attribute through the Microsoft 365 admin center (omit EffectiveDate ). Verify 100% coverage on Data Quality page. Phase 3: Create partitions filtered by Agency = "Agency A" , etc. Assign analysts. Phase 4: Analysts run Copilot PBI queries within their partition → publish reports. Time estimate: 2–3 days. Ongoing: Monthly CSV re-upload to keep data current.

heading: Path B: Entra ID Domain Filter (Zero CSV)
content: Use when: Each agency has a distinct email domain (e.g., agencya.gov.au , agencyb.gov.au ) All employees use their agency domain as their primary SMTP address You do not need custom attribute filtering (Department/Location come only from Entra defaults) You want the fastest possible deployment with zero data preparation Partition filter: Domain = "agencya.gov.au" End-to-end workflow: Phase 0: Pre-flight audit (same as Path A) Phase 1: Lockdown — disable AutoCxO, delegation, Agent Dashboard, Metrics Export (same as Path A) Phase 2: Skip CSV upload. Optionally enable ManagerId and Organization in "Configure Entra connection" for richer hierarchy and department data. Phase 3: Create partitions filtered by Domain = "agencya.gov.au" , etc. Assign analysts. Phase 4: Analysts run Copilot PBI queries within their partition → publish reports. Time estimate: 1 day (no CSV preparation for the partition filter). Ongoing: Monitor primary SMTP domains, transfers, exceptions, contractors, and shared-service identities; verify partition counts after changes.

heading: Decision Matrix
content: Question If Yes → Path Do all agencies share the same email domain? Path A (CSV required — Domain cannot differentiate agencies) Does each agency have a unique email domain? Path B is available (can also use Path A for richer attributes) Do you need Department/Location/Job Function filters per agency? Path A (CSV adds these attributes beyond Entra defaults) Are there shared-services staff on a common domain? Path A preferred (assign Agency = "Shared Services" in CSV) Need the fastest deployment with minimal data preparation? Path B (zero CSV, Domain-only filter) Want to start with Path B and add CSV later? Path B now, Path A later — you can always upload CSV to add richer attributes. Use the parallel data ingestion feature to keep Entra as source for ManagerId/Organization while adding custom attributes via CSV. Important: Whichever path you choose, the group-scoped surface restrictions , partition assignment governance, Power BI controls, and evidence gate are the same. The path changes how organizational data reaches Viva Insights and which attribute scopes the analyst query workspace.

heading: Copilot Analytics with Agency-Default Views for Multi-Agency Single Tenant
content: Version: 1.2 | Author: Sumit Sadhu | Last validated: 2 October 2026 THIS GUIDE'S AUTHOR-CREATED ARCHITECTURE PATTERN Default Priority is an editorial name created by this guide. It is not a Microsoft product, security, compliance, sovereignty, or licensing term. The companion Restricted Reporting pattern was formerly labelled "Isolation"; the old word remains in the existing filename and URL only for link stability. Microsoft documents the component capabilities, but does not document either combined pattern as an end-to-end security boundary. This pattern intentionally accepts that some authorized users can obtain broader cross-agency or tenant-wide views. Manager hierarchy can establish a useful default scope, but it is not an authorization boundary. Viva Insights partitions limit rows and columns in an assigned analyst query workspace; separate controls govern Dashboard, Analytics Reports, Agent Dashboard, metrics export, delegation, manager access, privileged roles, downloaded results, and Power BI. Neither pattern creates cryptographic, tenant, product-security, or independently certified isolation.

heading: 1. Executive Summary
content: This document provides an author-created reporting pattern for a single Microsoft 365 tenant that hosts multiple agencies , where each agency wants to see its own Copilot adoption and impact data by default and explicitly accepts broader authorized cross-agency or tenant-wide visibility. Key Difference from Restricted Reporting: Restricted Reporting applies group-scoped restrictions and partitioned analyst workspaces to reduce cross-agency reporting paths. This guide keeps eligible native features available because broader authorized visibility is accepted. Hierarchy provides a default view, not a security boundary. Recommended Approach: Native Scoping + Optional Partitions Copilot Dashboard with "Your group" scope — agency leaders auto-identified; "Your group" shows their own hierarchy's data (which scope the dashboard opens to is not stated by Microsoft — confirm in the tenant). Dashboard Delegation — CEOs delegate to VPs and directors for agency-scoped views; a delegate can't delegate further. The prompts guide you to the next step automatically. Prompt 1: Data Readiness    Prompt 2: Dashboard Impact    Prompt 3: Remediation Plan First time? Read the report it produces and save it (for example, copy it into a Word or text document). Repeat steps 3–5 for Prompt 2 , then Prompt 3 — attaching the same file each time.
